arxiv-2210-00327.title: Deep Recurrent Q-learning for Energy-constrained Coverage with a Mobile Robot
arxiv-2210-00327.creator: Aaron Zellner, Ayan Dutta, Iliya Kulbaka, Gokarna Sharma
arxiv-2210-00327.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the problem of coverage of an environment with an energy-constrained robot in the presence of multiple charging stations. As the robot’s on-board power supply is limited, it might not have enough energy to cover all the points in the environment with a single charge.

arxiv-2303-17018.title: System Predictor: Grounding Size Estimator for Logic Programs under Answer Set Semantics
arxiv-2303-17018.creator: DANIEL BRESNAHAN, NICHOLAS HIPPEN, YULIYA LIERLER
arxiv-2303-17018.description: Abstract Answer set programming is a declarative logic programming paradigm geared towards solving difficult combinatorial search problems. While different logic programs can encode the same problem, their performance may vary significantly. It is not always easy to identify which version of the program performs the best.

arxiv-2306-16290.title: Inhomogeneous condensation in the Gross-Neveu model in noninteger spatial dimensions 1 ≤ d < 3 1\leq d<3
arxiv-2306-16290.creator: Laurin Pannullo
arxiv-2306-16290.description: Abstract The Gross-Neveu model in the N → ∞ N\to\infty limit in d = 1 d=1 spatial dimensions exhibits a chiral inhomogeneous phase (IP), where the chiral condensate has a spatial dependence that spontaneously breaks translational invariance and the ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} chiral symmetry.

arxiv-2407-18311.title: Long-term radio monitoring of the fast X-ray transient EP240315a: evidence for a relativistic jet
arxiv-2407-18311.creator: Roberto Ricci, Eleonora Troja, Yu-Han Yang, Muskan Yadav, Yuan Liu, Hui Sun, Xuefeng Wu, He Gao, Bing Zhang, Weimin Yuan
arxiv-2407-18311.description: Abstract The recent launch of Einstein Probe (EP) in early 2024 opened up a new window onto the transient X-ray sky, allowing for real-time discovery and follow-up of fast X-ray transients (FXRTs). Multi-wavelength observations of FXRTs and their counterparts are key to characterize the properties of their outflows and, ultimately, identify their progenitors.

arxiv-2410-08541.title: Decomposing Infrared Luminosity Functions into Star-Forming and AGN Components using CIGALE
arxiv-2410-08541.creator: \gn Daniel J. \sn Lyon 1, \gn Michael J. \sn Cowley 1,2, \gn Oliver \sn Pye 1, and \gn Andrew M. \sn Hopkins 3
arxiv-2410-08541.description: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the infrared (IR) luminosity functions (LF) of star-forming (SF) galaxies and active galactic nuclei (AGN) using data from the ZFOURGE survey. We employ CIGALE to decompose the spectral energy distribution (SED) of galaxies into SF and AGN components to investigate the co-evolution of these processes at higher redshifts and fainter luminosities.

arxiv-2509-25428.title: Multi-year stacking searches for solar system bodies Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , Astroquery ( A. Ginsburg et al. 2019 ) , Matplotlib ( J. D. Hunter 2007 ) , numdifftools ( P. A. Brodtkorb 2025 ; J. D’Errico 2
arxiv-2509-25428.creator: Alex Geringer-Sameth, Nathan Golovich, Keita Iwabuchi
arxiv-2509-25428.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alex Geringer-Sameth, Nathan Golovich, Keita Iwabuchi. Digital tracking detects faint solar system bodies by stacking many images along hypothesized orbits, revealing objects that are undetectable in every individual exposure. Previous searches have been restricted to small areas and short time baselines. We present a general framework to quantify both sensitivity and computational requirements for digital tracking of nonlinear motion across the full sky over multi-year baselines.

arxiv-2605-05911.creator: Millend Roy, Agostino Capponi, Vineet Goyal

pmc-10508952.title: CHA2DS2-VASc score, P-wave indexes, and echocardiographic parameters in sinus rhythm patients without valvular heart disease
pmc-10508952.creator: Amanda Vanessa Demarchi, Luciana Vidal Armaganijan, Dalmo Antonio Ribeiro Moreira, Mariane Higa Shinzato, Kelvin Henrique Vilalva, Pablo Santos Graffitti, Rodrigo Augusto de Miranda Bertin, Mathias Antonio Haruno de Vilhena, Murilo Amato David, Guilherme Dagostin de Carvalho
pmc-10508952.description: SUMMARYOBJECTIVE:The aim of this study was to evaluate the correlation between P-wave indexes, echocardiographic parameters, and CHA2DS2-VASc score in patients without atrial fibrillation and valvular disease.METHODS:This retrospective cross-sectional study included patients of a tertiary hospital with no history of atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, or valve disease and collected data from June 2021 to May 2022.

pmc-10525276.title: Detection of Math6-Expressing Cell Types in Murine Placenta
pmc-10525276.creator: Maren Brendel, Marion Scharf, Urs Kindler, Satya Srirama Karthik Divvela, Beate Brand-Saberi
pmc-10525276.description: Simple SummaryThe protein, mouse atonal homolog 6 (Math6), is required for correct placental development in mice and causes loss of pregnancy, leading to reproductive insufficiency in females, when it is missing. It is currently unclear which cell types of the placenta predominantly express this protein.

pmc-10645381.title: Type I interferon signature and cycling lymphocytes in macrophage activation syndrome
pmc-10645381.creator: Zhengping Huang, Kailey E. Brodeur, Liang Chen, Du, Holly Wobma, Evan E. Hsu, Meng Liu, Joyce C. Chang, Margaret H. Chang, Janet Chou, Megan Day-Lewis, Fatma Dedeoglu, Olha Halyabar, James A. Lederer, Tianwang Li, Mindy S. Lo, Meiping Lu, Esra Meidan, Jane W. Newburger, Adrienne G. Randolph, Mary Be
pmc-10645381.description: BACKGROUNDMacrophage activation syndrome (MAS) is a life-threatening complication of Still’s disease (SD) characterized by overt immune cell activation and cytokine storm. We aimed to further understand the immunologic landscape of SD and MAS.METHODWe profiled PBMCs from people in a healthy control group and patients with SD with or without MAS using bulk RNA-Seq and single-cell RNA-Seq (scRNA-Seq).

pmc-11288350.title: Neonatal Tetanus Case Series: A Tale of Survival and Tragedy at St Paul Hospital Millennium Medical College, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
pmc-11288350.creator: Tigist Bacha, Mahlet Abayneh, Dawit Bekele Tefera
pmc-11288350.description: BackgroundNeonatal tetanus remains a significant threat in regions with limited healthcare access, despite being preventable through vaccination. The case-fatality rate of untreated neonatal tetanus is close to 100%. Even one case of neonatal tetanus regarded as a failure of the healthcare system, making it essential to remain mindful of this disease’s relevance to public health.

pmc-11417859.title: MicroRNA Profiling as a Predictive Indicator for Time to First Treatment in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia: Insights from the O-CLL1 Prospective Study
pmc-11417859.creator: Ennio Nano, Francesco Reggiani, Adriana Agnese Amaro, Paola Monti, Monica Colombo, Nadia Bertola, Fabiana Ferrero, Franco Fais, Antonella Bruzzese, Enrica Antonia Martino, Ernesto Vigna, Noemi Puccio, Mariaelena Pistoni, Federica Torricelli, Graziella D’Arrigo, Gianluigi Greco, Giovanni Tripepi, Car
pmc-11417859.description: A “watch and wait” strategy, delaying treatment until active disease manifests, is adopted for most CLL cases; however, prognostic models incorporating biomarkers have shown to be useful to predict treatment requirement. In our prospective O-CLL1 study including 224 patients, we investigated the predictive role of 513 microRNAs (miRNAs) on time to first treatment (TTFT).

pmc-11497745.title: Stakeholder Perspectives on Research, Policy and Practice Priorities to Increase Human Milk Feeding Rates in the United Kingdom
pmc-11497745.creator: Amy Elizabeth Burton, Alison Owen, Jennifer Taylor, Isobel Lindsay-Wiles, Joanna Heyes, Fiona Cust, Sarah Page
pmc-11497745.description: Background:Human milk feeding rates in the United Kingdom are a public health concern. Changes to United Kingdom policy and practice are needed to improve lactation support. These should be informed by those with lived experience of human milk feeding and those who provide support.

pmc-11530569.title: A Framework for the Use and Likelihood of Regulatory Acceptance of Single-Arm Trials
pmc-11530569.creator: Disha Subramaniam, Colin Anderson-Smits, Rebecca Rubinstein, Sydney T Thai, Rose Purcell, Cynthia Girman
pmc-11530569.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundSingle-arm clinical trials (SAT) are common in drug and biologic submissions for rare or life-threatening conditions, especially when no therapeutic options exist. External control arms (ECAs) improve interpretation of SATs but pose methodological and regulatory challenges.ObjectiveThrough narrative reviews and expert input, we developed a framework for considerations that might influence regulatory use and likelihood of regulatory acceptance of an SAT, identifying non-oncology first indication approvals as an area of interest. We systematically analyzed FDA and EMA approvals using SATs as pivotal evidence.

pmc-11591667.title: Development of a Recombinase Polymerase Amplification-Coupled CRISPR/Cas12a Platform for Rapid Detection of Antimicrobial-Resistant Genes in Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales
pmc-11591667.creator: Ji Woo Yang, Heesu Kim, Lee-Sang Hyeon, Jung Sik Yoo, Sangrim Kang
pmc-11591667.description: The worldwide spread of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) represents a significant threat owing to the high mortality and morbidity rates. Traditional diagnostic methods are often too slow and complex for rapid point-of-care testing. Therefore, we developed a recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA)-coupled CRISPR/Cas12a system (RCCS), a rapid, accurate, and simple diagnostic platform for detecting antimicrobial-resistant genes.

pmc-12151611.title: Directly Integrating Health Information Exchange (HIE) Data with the Electronic Health Record Increases HIE Use by Emergency Department Clinicians
pmc-12151611.creator: Rebecca L Rivera, Heidi Hosler, Jeong Hoon Jang, Jason T Schaffer, John Price, Joshua R Vest, Titus K Schleyer
pmc-12151611.description: ObjectivesThis article (1) develops a Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources app, Health Dart, that integrates information from Indiana’s community health information exchange (HIE), the Indiana Network for Patient Care (INPC), directly with Cerner, an electronic health record (EHR), and (2) evaluates the effect of Health Dart’s implementation on HIE use.

pmc-12559246.title: Experimental study on creep mechanical properties and failure modes of anthracite in dry and saturated states
pmc-12559246.creator: Xiaoqiang Zhang, Jianbing Yan, Kai Wang, Shaofei Yue, Fumin Zhang, Wenwei Wang
pmc-12559246.description: Water is crucial to the durability and safety of underground engineering. To investigate the effect of long-term goaf water infiltration on creep characteristics and long-term stability of the No.3 anthracite pillar in the Qinshui coalfield in Shanxi Province, conventional uniaxial compression and uniaxial creep tests were conducted under dry and saturated conditions.

pmc-12562301.title: Correction: An et al. Integrin β1-Mediated Cell−Cell Adhesion Augments Metformin-Induced Anoikis. Int. J. Mol. Sci. 2019, 20, 1161
pmc-12562301.creator: Tingting An, Zhiming Zhang, Yuhuang Li, Jianqiao Yi, Wenhua Zhang, Deshi Chen, Juan Ao, Zhi-Xiong Xiao, Yong Yi
pmc-12562301.description: d Figure 2 and Figure 3 appear below. The authors state that the scientific conclusions are unaffected. This correction was approved by the Academic Editor. The original publication has also been updated. Metformin induces expression of integrin β1 resulting in cell aggregation and promoting anoikis.

pmc-12662159.title: Equity Beyond Entry: A Capability Approach to Understanding Widening Participation in Medical Education
pmc-12662159.creator: Ashley Simpson, David Hope, Jeni Harden, Lorna Marson, Victoria Tallentire
pmc-12662159.description: Introduction:Widening participation aims to promote equity in medical education and build a more diverse healthcare workforce. Despite ongoing efforts, systemic inequities persist in shaping students’ trajectories. This study explores how widening participation students experience medical education, examining the factors that enable or constrain their success across the continuum of entry and progression.

pmc-13345675.title: Modeling Human Impact on the Distribution of the Only Existing Species of Euryale
pmc-13345675.creator: Yanxuan Li, Ningjing Zhang, Zhongyi Gao, Jiani Shi, Bingru Fang, Jishu Guo, Peng Xie, Yun Zhang, Wen Xiong, Kun Xu
pmc-13345675.description: Human activity has a profound impact on the distribution of a number of species, especially those with ecological and economic importance. Euryale ferox Salisb., an annual macrophyte native to South, Southeast, and East Asia, has long been cultivated for its fruits and seeds in north India and east China.

pmc-13401612.title: Pediatric Neck Impalement Injuries: A Report of Two Cases and Review of the Literature
pmc-13401612.creator: Ayaka Tsutsumi, Roxanna Hamidpour, Matthew Wagoner, Giovanni Ayala, Mehmet Erkilinc, Shin Miyata, Christopher Blewett
pmc-13401612.description: Penetrating neck impalement injuries in children are rare but potentially life-threatening. We present two cases to illustrate the clinical spectrum of this injury pattern and reinforce key management principles.Case 1 was a 13-year-old female patient who sustained a wooden stick impalement to the right neck during a sledding accident.

pmc-13516750.title: Research Priorities in Perioperative Nursing Across the Lifespan: An e-Delphi Consensus Study
pmc-13516750.creator: Ana Ramos, Rita Maurício, Sara Pires, Susana Mendonça, Lúcia Jerónimo, Hélder Fonseca, Piedade Pinto, Anabela Carvalho, Idalina Gomes, Eunice Sá, Carla Nascimento
pmc-13516750.description: Background/Objective: Perioperative nursing care encompasses a diverse patient population with varying needs, anatomical and physiological characteristics, and differing levels of vulnerability, demanding specialized knowledge and skills. This study aims to identify key research priorities in perioperative nursing across the lifespan.

pmc-13680266.title: Phenotyping persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn: recognition of its persistence across world symposium on pulmonary hypertension classifications
pmc-13680266.creator: Stephanie M Tsoi, Philip T Levy, Steven H Abman, Nidhy P Varghese
pmc-13680266.description: The earliest clinical sign of pulmonary vascular disease in neonates is persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN), traditionally classified as World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension (WSPH) Group 1. Typical PPHN is defined by the delayed transition from intra- to extra- uterine life with failure of pulmonary artery pressures to fall after delivery.
